On examination, he has tenderness in the right upper quadrant of his abdomen. Laboratory studies reveal an elevated serum amylase level. An abdominal CT scan shows pancreatic necrosis.  The most likely diagnosis for this patient is acute pancreatitis.  The pathophysiology of acute pancreatitis involves autodigestion of the pancreatic acinar cells by activated pancreatic enzymes. This activation can occur due to various causes, including alcohol use, which is the most common cause in this patient.  Alcohol can lead to the release of digestive enzymes from the pancreas prematurely, causing autodigestion and inflammation of the pancreatic tissue. This inflammation can result in the release of cytokines and other inflammatory mediators, leading to systemic inflammation.  The clinical presentation of acute pancreatitis includes severe epigastric pain that radiates to the back, nausea, vomiting, and fever.
